title: Personal pronouns and be
description: I am, you are, he is … – Personalpronomen und die Lang- und Kurzformen von be
subject: Englisch

categories.name: Welches Pronomen?
categories.description: Mia and I → we, the bike → it …

categories.name: Kurzformen
categories.description: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're

questions.explanation: Eine andere Person + ich = wir → we.
Dinge sind im Englischen immer it – auch wenn es im Deutschen "das", "der" oder "die" heißt.
Mehrere Personen ohne dich und mich → they.
Die Schultasche ist ein Ding → it (nicht she wie "sie" im Deutschen).

questions.prompt: Our dog's name is Bruno. ___ is very friendly.
questions.explanation: Ein Haustier mit Namen kann he oder she sein. Bruno ist ein Rüde → he.

questions.prompt: Look, there's a spider on the wall! ___ is black.
questions.explanation: Fremde Tiere ohne Namen sind it.

questions.prompt: Which word is always written with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: I (ich) schreibt man immer groß – auch mitten im Satz.

questions.prompt: Lena talks to her two brothers: "___ are funny!" (ihr)
questions.explanation: you heißt du, ihr und Sie – immer dasselbe Wort.
Zu I gehört immer am.
he, she, it → is.
we, you, they → are.
the cat = it → is.

questions.prompt: Ben and Lena ___ at the swimming pool. (Langform)
questions.explanation: Ben and Lena = they → are, nicht is.
my parents = they → are.
Auch wenn you nur eine Person (du) meint: you → are.
football = it → is.

questions.text: I {am} in Munich. My grandma {is} here too. We {are} at the zoo.
questions.explanation: I → am, he/she/it → is, we/you/they → are.

questions.text: Ms Carter {is} our teacher. Her lessons {are} fun. The classroom {is} big.
questions.explanation: Ms Carter = she → is, her lessons = they → are, the classroom = it → is.
Der Apostroph ersetzt das fehlende a: I'm.
Der Apostroph ersetzt das fehlende a: they're.
we're (wir sind) mit Apostroph – nicht verwechseln mit were.
it's = it is – der Apostroph darf nicht fehlen.

questions.prompt: Which short form is correct for "you are"?
questions.explanation: you're = you are. your = dein/euer.

questions.prompt: Which short form is correct for "he is"?
questions.explanation: he's = he is. his = sein.

questions.prompt: "We are" is the long form. What is the short form?
questions.explanation: Bei der Kurzform fällt der erste Buchstabe von are weg: we're.

questions.text: I am → {I'm}, he is → {he's}, you are → {you're}, they are → {they're}
questions.explanation: Der Apostroph steht genau dort, wo ein Buchstabe fehlt.

questions.text: {I'm} Noah. {She's} my friend Mia. {We're} in the school band.
questions.explanation: Kurzformen brauchen immer einen Apostroph.

questions.text: Hi, {I'm} Lena. This is my rabbit, Snowy. {She's} white and very cute.
questions.explanation: Ein Haustier mit Namen kann he oder she sein: Snowy → She's. Kurzformen brauchen einen Apostroph.

questions.text: My bike is new. {It's} red. My friends {are} at the park.
questions.explanation: Das Fahrrad ist ein Ding → It's. my friends = they → are.

questions.text: Ben is my cousin. {He} is twelve. Mia and I are in class 5a. {We} are eleven.
questions.explanation: Ben → He, Mia and I → We.

questions.text: Hello, Ms Carter. How {are} you? I {am} fine, thanks. My mum {is} fine too.
questions.explanation: you → are (auch bei Sie), I → am, my mum = she → is.

options: Noah and I are in the team.
Noah and I is in the team.
Noah and i are in the team.
Noah and I am in the team.
questions.answer: Noah and I are in the team.
questions.explanation: Noah and I = we → are. I schreibt man immer groß.

options: My pencil case is blue. It's new.
My pencil case is blue. She's new.
My pencil case is blue. Its new.
My pencil case is blue. It are new.
questions.answer: My pencil case is blue. It's new.
questions.explanation: Ein Ding ist it, und it is wird zu it's – mit Apostroph.

questions.prompt: Max and Ben are my friends. ___ are in my class. (Pronomen)
questions.explanation: Max and Ben = they.

questions.prompt: This is Oma Rosi. ___ seventy years old. (Pronomen + be, Kurzform)
questions.explanation: Oma Rosi ist eine Frau → she is → She's.

questions.prompt: Hello, Mr Weber! ___ my new teacher. (Pronomen + be, Kurzform)
questions.explanation: Mr Weber wird direkt angesprochen → you are → You're (nicht your).
